data.body:
Landed as Gerrit change 1133, merged 2d0827b84df43587eabbc0c612c3924e0cc57b0b.

AC1 — HEALTH_TIMEOUT default 30 -> 120, justified against the app's own budgets rather than picked arbitrarily. The dominant term is the store write lock taken by run_ensures(): _store/lock.py _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (30) x _DEFAULT_ATTEMPTS (2) = 60s spent before it logs 'write lock unavailable, skipping sweep' and continues. Corroborated in-repo: the container entrypoint runs infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh:65 (run_ensures) BEFORE 'exec uvicorn', so that budget is spent while /health cannot answer at all. The readiness loop adds up to 5s of granularity (sleep 2 + curl -m 3), so ~65s is the floor; 120s is 2x the dominant budget. Still env-overridable (proven behaviourally by the tests, which drive the script with HEALTH_TIMEOUT=1).

AC2 — a bot-unhealthy failure now captures a bounded tail of the failing container's own output into the deploy journal BEFORE the rollback replaces that container. Bounded three ways (HEALTH_FAIL_LOG_LINES=100, HEALTH_FAIL_LOG_BYTES=20000, timeout 15) and strictly best-effort. The captured text has the literal AUTODEPLOY_ERROR token redacted: observability.sh:169 counts lines carrying it in this unit's journal to drive the deploy_errors CloudWatch alarm, so an unredacted echo of container output could inflate the alarm — regression-tested.

AC3 — the fail-safe guarantee is unchanged and now regression-tested rather than merely asserted: :prev is re-tagged :latest, the service is restarted after the re-tag, a SHA-keyed backoff is recorded, and deployed-sha does not advance.

Tests: tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_health_gate.py (4 tests). Confirmed RED first and given teeth by mutation — reverting the default to 30, removing the capture call, and removing the redaction each return the corresponding test to RED. Runbook updated (infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md) with a 'Diagnosing bot-unhealthy' entry.

No production host was touched.
